slides.title: The Frame — Why These Two Cards

items.text: Sooner or later, everyone who walks with God hits a dry season — and the dangerous thing is not the dryness, it is the wrong diagnosis
The Signs Card — so a misread dry season never ends a journey in this room
The Path Home Card — the written door back, and it ends the way Luke 15 ends: the father runs
Tonight is a rehearsal — the small room before the large one. Your cluster is their first congregation.
At the end, your cluster gives its teacher two gifts: one thing to keep, and one thing to adjust
Tonight is about the cards, not anyone’s current season — nobody will be asked where they are

panel.label: 2 TIMOTHY 2:2
lines: “and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.”
Four generations in one sentence — Paul, Timothy, the faithful, and the others also. Tonight you are watching the third handoff happen.

items.text: Each cluster named — its families, its adult, its first-round Companion-in-Formation
Pray — for the teachers by name, and for any dry ground in the room, unnamed
Then split — receive your teacher, and work the cards with them
The Signs Card (~13 min) — the one question: “Which way does the desire point?” Then the four kinds of dry, from the card’s own table
Cases 3 and 4 — one says resist, the other says receive; opposite motions. When you cannot tell which you are in, do not decide alone.
The Path Home Card (~10 min) — the five steps, and the reception: it ends with a feast, not a hearing
“The door is not locked. The light is on.”
Close (~2 min) — both cards go home tonight; this week your family gives them a findable spot
Questions of information are welcome — the teacher answers them. The adults hold every door that opens.

panel.label: LUKE 15:20
lines: “while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran”

slides.title: Cluster Feedback — One Keep, One Adjust

items.text: The adult models first — one specific keep, one specific adjust
Specific means quotable: “keep the way you paused after the desire question” — not “you did great”
Then a parent adds one; one or two more voices if brief — teens welcome
The teacher receives without defending — “thank you” is the whole response
Both gifts go on the note sheet — this block is the reason the evening exists

slides.title: Second Teaching Rep — Both Cards, Tightened

items.text: “Teachers, travel.” Each teacher moves one cluster over, adjust in hand — the new cluster is a clean room
The same arc, compressed — Signs ~11 min, Path Home ~8, close ~1
The compression is the second rep’s own skill — same spine, fewer words, the load-bearing minutes untouched
The desire question — resist versus receive — the father runs
The adjust from Round 1 gets tried here, while it is warm
Same shape, briefer — the adult’s keep and adjust, then one cluster voice
The keep, wherever honest, names the adjust that got tried
Both recorded per teacher — these notes are next week’s prep meeting
One practice this week — the easiest assignment of the year: the two cards go home and get a spot
Somewhere findable — a drawer everyone knows about, the kitchen cabinet door, inside the family Bible. Decide the spot together.
If all goes well, they will sit there gathering dust for years. That is the job — the cards wait.
Next Wednesday is The Long Walk — the whole room, the whole teaching, these same teachers. Come ready to receive them again.
